messages:
emily_pm: quick check — i put together a short PRD/RFC outline for the SDK streaming client work we talked about. primary goals: ergonomic API, predictable backoff, and telemetry for deadline misses. can we align scope for the next sprint?

sara_devex: pinged — saw the doc. can you paste the acceptance criteria here? want to make sure we don't over-index on features for launch.

emily_pm: pasted below (high level):
- must: streaming client supports graceful reconnect + resume semantics for transient network errors
- must: default exponential backoff with jitter and an easy opt-out surface
- must: per-request deadline metadata surfaced to telemetry + metric for deadline_exceeded
- should: client exposes an ergonomics layer for common patterns (single-call streaming, chunked responses)
- could: auto-hedging toggles for high-P99 latency flows (opt-in for now)

raj_eng: couple clarifying q's: 1) "resume semantics" = resuming from last acknowledged token or just reconnect + replay? 2) telemetry: are we sending token counts or just event markers?

emily_pm: good qs — intent is reconnect + resume using server-side KV cache when available (fall back to replay otherwise). telemetry should start with event markers (connect, reconnect, resume, deadline_exceeded) + optional token delta if SDK opts in. keep costs low by default.

mike_platform: for Dedicated/private we need a knob to disable telemetry export defaults (org policy). add config: telemetry.enabled = true/false and telemetry.level = minimal|detailed. also add a hook for custom exporters.

sara_devex: ergonomics note: surface a single async iterator API for JS + a sync blocking iterator for Python (for simple use cases). advanced users can access low-level frames. keep retry/backoff config minimal: {maxRetries, baseMs, maxMs, jitter}.

raj_eng: implementation concerns: resume requires storing cursor state client-side when servers don't support KV cache. that'll impact memory usage on mobile. propose a small disk-backed option for mobile SDKs — or we document tradeoffs and ship without disk persistence.

emily_pm: decision needed: ship with in-memory resume only and document mobile limitation, or add a low-effort persistence layer for mobile in this sprint?

sara_devex: i'd prefer in-memory only for initial launch to reduce surface area. add acceptance criteria: doc callouts for mobile, and an issue to add persistence in Q2.

mike_platform: agree. also add rollout criteria: canary with <1% of traffic, metrics: reconnect_rate, resume_success_rate, deadline_exceed_rate, and a latency SLO check.

emily_pm: good. acceptance checklist for RFC:
- API sketches for JS/Py (iterator patterns + low-level hooks)
- default retry/backoff params + how to override
- telemetry event schema + env knobs for Dedicated/Private
- server compatibility matrix (resume w/kv, replay-only)
- migration notes for existing non-streaming clients
- launch gating metrics and rollback plan

raj_eng: i'll draft the API sketches and async iterator examples. sara, can you draft the public-facing docs and quickstart? mike, can you spec the env knobs for Dedicated/Private? i'll add a small perf test plan.

sara_devex: yup. i'll also write a short snippet for the README and add code samples that show default vs advanced usage.

ci-bot: reminder: RFC template checklist updated. please link the RFC PR early to get automated linting.

emily_pm: timeline: aim to have RFC ready for review by Tue (48h). Sprint planning will decide shipping sprint but plan for canary in next minor release.

mike_platform: noted. blocking items: a small infra workitem to expose telemetry.disable_env. i'll open a ticket.

sara_devex: ok, i'll carve out docs work for friday.

emily_pm: thanks all — i'll start the RFC PR and tag you. if anyone has major scope pushback call it out now, otherwise we'll lock in in-memory resume + minimal telemetry for launch. :thumbsup:
